Case: Dustin is a 25-year-old who is post-op day 4 status-post suboccipital craniectomy for Chiari type-1 malformation. The surgery was uncomplicated, however Dustin experienced severe nausea and vomiting for 2 days after surgery. Dustin now feels better, and he says that his headaches have improved, but he is having a lot of pain at his suboccipital incision site. On physical examination, he has no neurological deficits, and his surgical site and posterior neck are tender to palpation. A post-operative MRI confirms adequate decompression of his Chiari malformation and no hydrocephalus. Per the medication administration record, he has required some hydrocodone every 8 hours for pain control.
Question: Would you offer a hydrocodone prescription to Dustin? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
